1.explanation: The root of the bug is in the MAGIC_COMMENT definition inside the default exported function in latex.js. It uses a case-sensitive literal begin:'% !TeX', so lines with uppercase !TEX do not match and fall back to the generic COMMENT rule. To fix the issue, the MAGIC_COMMENT begin pattern must be changed to a case-insensitive or regex variant (e.g. /% !TeX/i or /% !TeX/i) so that both !TeX and !TEX trigger the meta class.
1.bug_scenario: In the LaTeX highlight preview (first screenshot) both magic-comment lines “% !TeX program = lualatex” and “% !TEX encoding = UTF-8” appear, but only the first (mixed-case “TeX”) is styled with the MAGIC_COMMENT rule. The all-uppercase “TEX” line remains a plain COMMENT. In the expected output (second screenshot) both lines should be highlighted as MAGIC_COMMENT, since TeX magic comments are case-insensitive.

2.explanation: The MAGIC_COMMENT constant in src/languages/latex.js defines a begin pattern of '% !TeX' (case-sensitive string) to detect TeX magic comments. Because it isn’t using a case-insensitive regular expression, lines like '% !TEX encoding = UTF-8' don’t match and fall back to the generic COMMENT rule. Updating MAGIC_COMMENT (for example to use a regex with the 'i' flag or a pattern like /% !TeX/i) will ensure magic comments are recognized regardless of case.
2.bug_scenario: The LaTeX highlighter’s “magic comment” rule only matches “% !TeX” with that exact casing. In the screenshots, “% !TeX program = lualatex” is highlighted correctly, but “% !TEX encoding = UTF-8” (uppercase “TEX”) is treated as a plain comment. Magic comments in most TeX editors are case-insensitive, so both lines should be highlighted as MAGIC_COMMENT.
